# Priscilla Grant

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c16 P14](../source/v02-c16.md#nw-v02-c16-p0014), [v3 c4 P6](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0006), [v3 c4 P31](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0031)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c3 P15](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0015)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** dream girl  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004)</sub>; Prissy  <sub>[v3 c3 P14](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0014)</sub>; Pris  <sub>[v3 c6 P12](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0012), [v3 c9 P6](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0006), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P4](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0004)</sub>

## Appearance

Priscilla is a pale, spiritual-looking maiden with golden and fair attire, described as possessing an ethereal, golden beauty. She stands quite tall, being at least two inches taller than most people in a crowd.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c20 P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022), [v3 c4 P6](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0006), [v4 c1 P24](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0024)_

## Personality

Despite her ethereal appearance, Priscilla is full to the brim of mischief, pranks, and fun. She possesses a gay, cheerful demeanor that easily brightens up her companions, though she can also be resolute when setting house rules or giving straightforward advice.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c3 P24](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0024), [v3 c10 P56](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0056)_

## Goals

- wished to be famous  <sub>[v2 c13 P34](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0034)</sub>

## History

Priscilla attended Queen's Academy, where she became part of a close-knit circle of intimate friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. After graduating, she taught school in her home district. During her time on Prince Edward Island, she joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, preparing and reading a paper on cemeteries for one of their meetings. Later, she persuaded her father to let her attend Redmond College in Kingsport, arriving early to board with Anne Shirley. Along with Anne, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, she lived at Patty's Place while studying classics during her college years. Following her time at Redmond, Priscilla married a handsome, well-dressed foreign missionary who admired her beauty, and relocated with him to Japan.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c6 P5](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0005), [v2 c15 P23](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0023), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v3 c1 P21](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0021), [v3 c3 P10](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0010), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028), [v4 c1 P24](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0024), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

- attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard  <sub>[v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v3 c9 P7](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0007)</sub>

## Quotes

> I would wish to be famous  <sub>[v2 c13 P34](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0034)</sub>

> And your own is a white violet, with purple streaks in its heart  <sub>[v2 c13 P71](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0071)</sub>

> There’s just one more thing. You, Phil, as all Redmond knows, entertain callers almost every evening. Now, at Patty’s Place we can’t do that. We have decided that we shall be at home to our friends on Friday evenings only. If you come with us you’ll have to abide by that rule.  <sub>[v3 c10 P56](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0056)</sub>

> I shall have to fall back on another Professor Woodleigh quotation to express what it has done for me. You remember that he said in his address, ‘There is so much in the world for us all if we only have the eyes to see it, and the heart to love it, and the hand to gather it to ourselves—so much in men and women, so much in art and literature, so much everywhere in which to delight, and for which to be thankful.’ I think Redmond has taught me that in some measure, Anne.  <sub>[v3 c37 P23](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0023)</sub>
